verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const r="app/q/[slug]/route.ts",f="components/spaces/qr-splash-form.tsx";if(!fs.existsSync(r)||!fs.existsSync(f)){console.error("SCAN-780: a file the probe must read is missing");process.exit(79)}const route=fs.readFileSync(r,"utf8"),form=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");const alwaysRedirects=/const cta = primarySplashLink\(splash\)\s*\n\s*if \(cta\) \{\s*\n\s*return withReferral\(NextResponse\.redirect/.test(route);const copyPromisesLanding=/A splash is a small landing page a scan lands on/.test(form);if(alwaysRedirects&&copyPromisesLanding){console.error("SCAN-780: the splash editor still promises a landing page with a heading, a blurb, an image and several links, but the /q resolver redirects every scan straight to the first link whenever one exists, so none of that content is ever shown.");process.exit(1)}'

append.detail: The /q resolver redirected every scan to links[0] whenever a splash had any link, so a heading, blurb, image and links two to five the owner authored were never shown, while the editor copy promised a landing page. Added the pure splashRedirectLink(splash) in lib/qr/splash.ts: it returns the link only for a bare single-link splash (one link, no blurb, no image); otherwise null. app/q/[slug]/route.ts now redirects only on that shortcut and renders renderSplashPage (first link styled as the main button) for everything else; lib/library/splash-registry.ts reads the same helper so its target label matches. Pinned by lib/qr/splash.test.ts (four splashRedirectLink cases) and app/q/[slug]/route.test.ts (a multi-link splash with blurb and image returns a 200 HTML landing carrying all of it; a bare single link still redirects).
